# Script introduction

Two maps for the manuscript, drawn from the outputs of earlier notebooks:

1. **The global geography of the strategies.** Comparable to Fig. 1 of `butterfly_ant_interactions`, on hexagons of about 210,000 km² (resolution 5 of `s05`) instead of 500-km squares, and drawn in the same style: hexagons clipped to the coastline, a light-blue sea, grey land where there is no estimate, country outlines on top and one high-contrast sequential palette (magma, light to dark) for every panel. The share of each strategy among the classified species of each hexagon with at least 10 classified species is shown on a square-root colour scale spanning the 1st to 99th percentiles of the panel's hexagons (so colours are not comparable between panels). The number of classified species and the share of recorded species that is classified (low in the Neotropics, tropical Africa and New Guinea) show where the maps rest on few species. The obligate species of each region by genus are drawn as a separate figure.
2. **The same climates, different strategies.** Every land pixel whose climate falls in a stratum occupied by the Mediterranean-climate parts of the Cape or southern Australia (`s13`), coloured by the obligate share of its region's species in these climates.

Design choices: Equal Earth projection for world maps. In both maps, as in the parent study, the sea is light blue and drawn over the hexagons (they are clipped to land), land without an estimate is mid-grey, and the colours come from one perceptually uniform palette that stays distinct from both. Direct labels instead of legends wherever possible.

A full run takes about 3 min.

## Packages

```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(resrepo)
library(data.table)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dggridR)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
```

## Variables

```{r setup_variables}
min_classified <- 10
strata_widths <- c(bio01 = 2, bio06 = 3, log_aridity = 0.15, bio15 = 15)
min_pixels <- 5
min_pool <- 5

region_levels <- c("Nearctic", "Neotropic", "Palearctic", "Tropical Africa", "Southern Africa",
                   "Indomalayan", "Australia", "New Guinea and islands")
region_short <- c(Nearctic = "Nearctic", Neotropic = "Neotropics", Palearctic = "Palaearctic",
                  `Tropical Africa` = "Tropical Africa", `Southern Africa` = "Southern Africa",
                  Indomalayan = "Indomalaya", Australia = "Australia",
                  `New Guinea and islands` = "New Guinea")
type_colours <- c(n = "#4D4D4D", f = "#0072B2", m = "#E69F00", p = "#CC79A7")
type_labels <- c(n = "Non-associated", f = "Facultative", m = "Obligate mutualist",
                 p = "Obligate parasite")

# Equal Earth, and the colours of land and empty land
crs_world <- "+proj=eqearth +datum=WGS84"
land_fill <- "#ECECEA"
land_line <- "#BDBDBA"

# Strategy maps in the style of Fig. 1 of butterfly_ant_interactions: light-blue sea over the
# hexagons, grey land without an estimate, dark country outlines, magma from light to dark
sea_fill <- "#ADD8E6"
empty_land <- "#8C8C8C"
border_line <- "#404040"
map_palette <- rev(viridisLite::magma(256, begin = 0.02, end = 0.98))
```

```{r define_helpers}
# World land, in Equal Earth
# World land without Antarctica, dissolved (planar geometry; the spherical union fails on this
# layer), in Equal Earth
world_land <- function() {
  sf_use_s2(FALSE)
  on.exit(sf_use_s2(TRUE))
  land <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf")
  land <- st_make_valid(land[land$continent != "Antarctica", "geometry"])
  st_transform(st_union(land), crs_world)
}

# Map extent in Equal Earth: Antarctica and the high Arctic are left out
map_ylim <- c(-6.2e6, 8.0e6)

# A sequential ramp of one hue, from light grey to the given colour
ramp_to <- function(colour, n = 5) colorRampPalette(c("#F2F2F0", colour))(n)

# Shared map theme
theme_map <- function(base_size = 8.5) {
  theme_void(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 0.5, hjust = 0.02),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
          legend.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5, colour = "grey30"),
          legend.key.height = unit(0.18, "cm"), legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
}

# Save a figure with ragg
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width, height, dpi = 300) {
  ggsave(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, bg = "white", device = ragg::agg_png)
}
```

# The global geography of the strategies

*Inputs:* s05/ cell_data_hex5.csv, hex_polygons.rds, species_regions.csv
*Outputs:* plot_world_strategies.png, plot_obligate_genera.png

```{r world_strategies}
cells <- fread(file.path(dir_s05, "cell_data_hex5.csv"))
hex <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s05, "hex_polygons.rds"))$hex5
hex <- st_wrap_dateline(hex, options = c("WRAPDATELINE=YES", "DATELINEOFFSET=180"))
hex <- merge(hex, cells, by.x = "seqnum", by.y = "cell_id")
hex <- st_transform(hex, crs_world)
land <- world_land()

# Hexagons clipped to land, so that the sea is drawn over their coastal parts (planar geometry in
# Equal Earth); country outlines are drawn on top
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
hex <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(st_make_valid(hex), land))
countries <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf")
countries <- st_transform(st_make_valid(countries[countries$continent != "Antarctica",
                                                  "geometry"]), crs_world)
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# --- Colour scales as in Fig. 1 of butterfly_ant_interactions: square-root scales whose limits
# span the 1st to 99th percentiles of the panel's cells, rounded outwards to 0.1; more extreme
# cells take the end colour, marked "≤" or "≥" in the legend ---
proportion_limits <- function(x) {
  q <- quantile(x[is.finite(x)], c(0.01, 0.99), names = FALSE)
  c(max(0, floor(round(q[1] * 10, 6)) / 10), min(1, ceiling(round(q[2] * 10, 6)) / 10))
}
proportion_breaks <- function(limits, x) {
  inner <- if (limits[1] > 0) c(0.5, 0.7) else if (limits[2] <= 0.2) c(0.025, 0.05, 0.1) else
    if (limits[2] <= 0.4) c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2) else c(0.1, 0.2, 0.4)
  breaks <- sort(unique(c(limits[1], inner[inner > limits[1] & inner < limits[2]], limits[2])))
  labels <- paste0(format(100 * breaks, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE), "%")
  if (min(x, na.rm = TRUE) < limits[1]) labels[1] <- paste("≤", labels[1])
  if (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) > limits[2]) labels[length(labels)] <- paste("≥", labels[length(labels)])
  list(breaks = breaks, labels = labels)
}

# One hexagon map with a vertical colour bar at its right: light-blue sea with a white graticule,
# grey land, the clipped hexagons and the country outlines
map_hex <- function(d, title, colours = map_palette, trans = "identity", limits = NULL,
                    breaks = waiver(), labels = waiver()) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = land, fill = empty_land, colour = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = value), colour = NA) +
    geom_sf(data = countries, fill = NA, colour = border_line, linewidth = 0.08) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = colours, trans = trans, limits = limits, breaks = breaks,
                         labels = labels, oob = scales::squish, name = NULL,
                         guide = guide_colourbar(barwidth = unit(2.4, "mm"),
                                                 barheight = unit(22, "mm"))) +
    coord_sf(crs = crs_world, expand = FALSE, ylim = map_ylim) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_map() +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = sea_fill, colour = NA),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
          legend.position = "right", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"))
}

# --- A-D: the share of each strategy ---
classified <- hex[hex$n_classified >= min_classified, ]
share_map <- function(k) {
  d <- classified
  d$value <- d[[paste0("n_", k)]] / d$n_classified
  limits <- proportion_limits(d$value)
  scale <- proportion_breaks(limits, d$value)
  map_hex(d, type_labels[[k]], trans = "sqrt", limits = limits, breaks = scale$breaks,
          labels = scale$labels)
}

# --- E: classified species per hexagon; F: share of the recorded species classified ---
d <- hex[hex$n_classified > 0, ]
d$value <- d$n_classified
richness <- map_hex(d, "Classified species", trans = "log10", breaks = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100))
d <- hex[hex$n_total >= min_classified, ]
d$value <- d$n_classified / d$n_total
completeness <- map_hex(d, "Recorded species that are classified", limits = c(0, 1),
                        breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = scales::label_percent())

# --- Obligate species of each region by genus ---
sp <- fread(file.path(dir_s05, "species_regions.csv"))
ob <- sp[interaction_type %in% c("m", "p") & !is.na(region), .N, by = .(region, genus)]
ob[, rank := frank(-N, ties.method = "first"), by = region]
ob[, label := fifelse(rank <= 3, genus, "Other genera")]
obs <- ob[, .(N = sum(N), genera = .N), by = .(region, label)]
obs[, region_total := sum(N), by = region]
obs <- obs[region_total > 0]
obs[, `:=`(region = factor(region_short[region], rev(region_short[region_levels])),
           is_other = label == "Other genera")]
obs[, order := fifelse(is_other, 99L, frank(-N, ties.method = "first")), by = region]
setorder(obs, region, order)
obs[, `:=`(xmax = cumsum(N), xmin = cumsum(N) - N), by = region]
obs[, genus_label := fifelse(is_other, paste0(genera, " other genera"), label)]
regions_all <- data.table(region = factor(region_short[region_levels],
                                          rev(region_short[region_levels])))
lineages <- ggplot(obs) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = as.numeric(region) - 0.36,
                ymax = as.numeric(region) + 0.36, fill = is_other),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Segment labels only where the text fits (about 1.9 species per character at this width)
  geom_text(data = obs[N >= 1.9 * nchar(genus_label)],
            aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = as.numeric(region),
                                     label = genus_label,
                                     fontface = ifelse(is_other, "plain", "italic")),
            size = 2.2, colour = "white") +
  geom_text(data = unique(obs[, .(region, region_total)]),
            aes(x = region_total, y = as.numeric(region), label = region_total),
            hjust = -0.3, size = 2.4, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = type_colours[["m"]], `TRUE` = "#F2C46D"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(levels(obs$region)), labels = levels(obs$region),
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Obligate species (three largest genera named)", y = NULL,
       title = "Few genera carry the obligate associates") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8.5) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "grey25"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "grey40"),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9), plot.title.position = "plot")

fig <- wrap_plots(share_map("n"), share_map("f"), share_map("m"), share_map("p"), richness,
                  completeness, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a", tag_prefix = "(", tag_suffix = ")") & theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
save_figure(fig, "plot_world_strategies", 7.4, 4.9)
save_figure(lineages, "plot_obligate_genera", 5, 2.6)
fig
```

# The same climates, different strategies

The climate strata of `s13` occupied (at least `r min_pixels` pixels) by the Mediterranean-climate pixels of the Cape or southern Australia are found anywhere on land. In each biogeographic region, the pool is every classified species recorded in its pixels of these strata, and the pixels are coloured by the pool's obligate share (regions with fewer than `r min_pool` classified species in grey).

*Inputs:* s13/ pixel_strata.rds, record_pixels.rds, taxa.csv; s01/climate_present_10m.tif
*Outputs:* shared_climate_pools.csv, plot_shared_climates.png, plot_shared_climates_panel.png

```{r shared_climates}
pix <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s13, "pixel_strata.rds"))
rec <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s13, "record_pixels.rds"))
taxa <- fread(file.path(dir_s13, "taxa.csv"), colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
target <- unique(pix[med_region %in% c("Cape", "Southern Australia"), .N,
                     by = .(med_region, stratum)][N >= min_pixels]$stratum)
tp <- pix[stratum %in% target & !is.na(region)]
pools <- rbindlist(lapply(region_levels, function(rg) {
  keys <- unique(rec[cell %in% tp[region == rg]$cell]$pool_key)
  t <- taxa[pool_key %in% keys & classified == TRUE]
  data.table(region = rg, pixels = tp[region == rg, .N], classified = nrow(t),
             obligate = sum(t$obligate), obligate_share = if (nrow(t)) mean(t$obligate) else NA)
}))
write_table(pools, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "shared_climate_pools.csv"))
print(pools, digits = 2)

# --- Hexagons (resolution 6, about 70,000 km²) holding target pixels, coloured by the obligate
# share of the region holding most of their target pixels; the pixels alone are too small to
# see on a world map ---
template <- rast(file.path(dir_s01, "climate_present_10m.tif"))[["bio01"]]
dg <- dgconstruct(res = 6)
xy <- xyFromCell(template, tp$cell)
tp[, hex := dgGEO_to_SEQNUM(dg, xy[, 1], xy[, 2])$seqnum]
hx <- tp[, .(target_pixels = .N, region = names(which.max(table(region)))), by = hex]
hx <- hx[target_pixels >= min_pixels]
hx <- merge(hx, pools[, .(region, obligate_share, classified)], by = "region")
hx[classified < min_pool, obligate_share := NA]
polys <- st_wrap_dateline(dgcellstogrid(dg, hx$hex),
                          options = c("WRAPDATELINE=YES", "DATELINEOFFSET=180"))
polys <- st_transform(merge(polys, hx, by.x = "seqnum", by.y = "hex"), crs_world)
land <- world_land()

# As in the strategy maps: hexagons clipped to land under a light-blue sea, country outlines on top
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
polys <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(st_make_valid(polys), land))
countries <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf")
countries <- st_transform(st_make_valid(countries[countries$continent != "Antarctica",
                                                  "geometry"]), crs_world)
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# Labels of the regions at the centroid of their target pixels
lab <- merge(tp[, .(x = mean(xyFromCell(template, cell)[, 1]),
                    y = mean(xyFromCell(template, cell)[, 2])), by = region],
             pools, by = "region")
lab <- lab[classified >= min_pool]
lab_sf <- st_transform(st_as_sf(lab, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326), crs_world)
lab[, c("X", "Y") := as.data.table(st_coordinates(lab_sf))]
lab[, text := paste0(region_short[region], "\n", round(100 * obligate_share), "% obligate (n = ",
                     classified, ")")]
# Labels moved off the hexagons, mostly into the sea, with a leader line (metres, Equal Earth)
offsets <- data.table(region = region_levels,
                      dx = c(-0.3e6, -2.6e6, -3.4e6, 2.6e6, -3.0e6, 3.0e6, -1.6e6, 0),
                      dy = c(-1.8e6, 0, 0.9e6, -0.4e6, -0.5e6, -0.6e6, 1.7e6, 0))
lab <- merge(lab, offsets, by = "region")
lab[, `:=`(LX = X + dx, LY = Y + dy)]

shared <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = empty_land, colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = polys[!is.na(polys$obligate_share), ], aes(fill = obligate_share),
          colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = polys[is.na(polys$obligate_share), ], fill = "#C8C8C8", colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = countries, fill = NA, colour = border_line, linewidth = 0.08) +
  geom_segment(data = lab, aes(x = X, y = Y, xend = LX, yend = LY), colour = "grey15",
               linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_label(data = lab, aes(LX, LY, label = text), size = 2.2, label.size = 0,
             fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.9), lineheight = 0.9,
             label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines")) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = map_palette, limits = c(0, 0.5),
                       oob = scales::squish, labels = scales::label_percent(),
                       name = "Obligate associates among the classified species of the region in these climates") +
  coord_sf(crs = crs_world, expand = FALSE, ylim = c(-5.2e6, 6.6e6), xlim = c(-1.25e7, 1.65e7)) +
  labs(title = "Climates like those of the Cape and southern Australia, and how obligate-rich they are",
       subtitle = "Hexagons with land in the climate strata of the Mediterranean-climate Cape or southern Australia; light grey: fewer than 5 classified species") +
  theme_map() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = sea_fill, colour = NA),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 7.5, hjust = 0.02),
        legend.key.width = unit(2.5, "cm"), legend.title.position = "top")
save_figure(shared, "plot_shared_climates", 9, 5.2)

# --- The same map as a panel of the paper's Figure 2: printed width, larger labels, no title ---
shared_panel <- shared +
  geom_label(data = lab, aes(LX, LY, label = text), size = 3, label.size = 0,
             fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.9), lineheight = 0.9,
             label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines")) +
  labs(title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = map_palette, limits = c(0, 0.5),
                       oob = scales::squish, labels = scales::label_percent(),
                       name = "Obligate share of the classified species of each region in these climates") +
  theme_map(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = sea_fill, colour = NA),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.key.width = unit(2.2, "cm"), legend.title.position = "top",
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
shared_panel$layers[[6]] <- NULL
save_figure(shared_panel, "plot_shared_climates_panel", 7.5, 4.3)
shared
```
